messages.subject: This week: Using bbmle and mle2 to estimate model parameters
messages.subject_clean: This week: Using bbmle and mle2 to estimate model parameters
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

This week at D-RUG Dave Harris will give a presentation about model-fitting with bbmle and mle2.  From Dave:

> Estimating parameters for ecological models: While many statistical models have pre-written programs for fitting them (e.g. glms), ecologists are often interested in fitting more mechanistic models.  This talk will focus on using Ben Bolker's bbmle package and the mle2 function to estimate model parameters.  Examples will probably include:
>
> * finding the attack rate and handling time in a foraging model
> * finding the growth rate and carrying capacity in a fisheries model.
>
> I'll also talk briefly about extracting confidence intervals from these models and some common pitfalls using the package.

We'll meet at the usual time and place: 2124 Wickson, Thursday 1pm-3pm.  This will be our last meeting until the fall!

Cheers,

Noam

Whoops! That should be install_github not install_gitub. require(devtools)
install_github("rethinking", "rmcelreath")

Hi all,

Thanks to everyone who filled out the D-RUG survey.  The results are quite useful.  Here are some of the main takeaways:

 - There was lots of interest in a summer work sessions.  I'll send another e-mail asking for times people want.
 - No one activity or resource (help, talks, email, blog) was most useful to people
 - Speakers were the biggest draw for work sessions.  Schedule conflicts were the biggest reason for non-attendance.  I'm not sure what to do about this as schedule conflicts are inevitable with a big group. There was a suggestion that we webcast.  I'll consider it.
 - There was some interest in moving to a once-every-two-weeks schedule.  I think in the fall, we will still have weekly help sessions, but only schedule speakers every other week.  It's tough to fill all the weekly slots, anyway.

You can view the complete results (minus emails) here: http://goo.gl/WXXkx

Noam

Are you using the raster package? I think a combination of the commands `zonal` and `area` from that package would work. My suggested pseudocode below, assuming your image is stored in a raster layer `x`

1. from `x` create a new rasterlayer `z` with each cell entry corresponding to the probability
2. use raster math on `z` to group the entries into appropriate bins of probability, e.g. z[z < 0.1] =0.1
3. run `area` on `x`, e.g.,
> a <- area(x)
4. use `zonal` to summarize area by probability bin
> zonal(a, z)
